title: How do you network for consulting jobs without feeling awkward?
description: A kind, practical guide to networking for consulting: who to contact, what to say, good questions to ask, and how to follow up.
hook: Networking can feel uncomfortable, especially if you do not come from a family or school with consulting contacts. Try thinking of it differently: you are simply having curious conversations with people about their jobs. Most consultants were helped by someone once and are happy to return the favour.
body:
Why it helps

  • You learn what each firm is really like, which helps you choose.
  • You collect specific details for your "why this firm" answer.
  • Some firms consider referrals or recommendations from their people.

Who to contact

  • Alumni from your university or previous employers (LinkedIn's alumni search helps).
  • People you meet at firm events, presentations and campus sessions.
  • Friends of friends. A warm introduction always beats a cold message.

A short message that works

Hi Priya, I'm a final-year economics student at Leeds and I'm exploring consulting. I saw you moved from engineering into strategy at your firm, which is a path I'm considering. Would you have 15 minutes for a call in the next few weeks? I'd love to hear how you found the move.

Good questions to ask

  • What surprised you most when you joined?
  • What kind of projects have you enjoyed most?
  • How would you describe the culture in your office?
  • What do you wish you had known before you applied?

Follow up

Send a thank-you message the same day, mentioning something specific they said. If you apply, let them know. Keep it light; you are building a relationship, not asking for a job.

Sources

  • Leland: How to get an interview at Bain

Checked November 2026.
